experiments.title: Batch robots into two InstancedMesh groups with corrected transform math and per-instance semantic IDs
experiments.hypothesis: The dominant cost is 1600 repeated opaque robot meshes causing 1611 draw calls. Replacing them with two InstancedMesh batches split by original material/color should collapse those robot submissions to two draw calls while preserving exact world transforms, colors, animation, and picking identity through userData.semanticIds.
experiments.expectedEffect: Large reduction in draw calls and CPU submission time, with identical robot placement and animation at every timestamp. Raycasting/picking identity remains available per instance via instanceId -> userData.semanticIds mapping.
experiments.notes: This is a focused repair of the previously rejected instancing attempt. The earlier patch changed transform arithmetic, causing visual/state/picking failures. This version preserves the original constants and expressions exactly: x uses (column - 19.5) * 1.25, y uses .32 + Math.sin(t * 1.8 + i * .13) * .04, z uses (row - Math.floor(count / 40) / 2) * 1.3 + Math.sin(t * .4 + column * .2) * .4, and rotation.y uses Math.sin(t * .5 + i * .04) * .18. Robots are batched only by their original opaque material split, which should cut robot draw submissions from 1600 to 2 while preserving per-instance semantic identity via userData.semanticIds.

experiments.title: No further safe draw-call reduction remains in src/scene.js
experiments.hypothesis: The dominant draw-call optimization for this file has already been accepted: batching 1600 repeated robots into two InstancedMesh groups by material. Within the allowed file, there is no additional safe batching opportunity that would reduce draw calls further without changing materials/colors or violating identity/semantic preservation.
experiments.expectedEffect: No source changes. Current accepted implementation already reduces robot submissions from ~1600 meshes to 2 instanced draws while preserving transforms and picking identity. Further edits in this file would be arithmetic/allocation variants, which do not meet the selected goal of reducing draw calls.
experiments.notes: History shows the accepted instancing patch is already present in src/scene.js, with calls reduced to 13 and correctness passing. Merging the two instanced groups into one draw would require changing the per-instance material/color model, which would alter the semantic material/color contract unless shader structure is expanded beyond the original contract. No other repeated opaque object set is visible in the allowed source. Repeating the accepted patch is disallowed, and non-batching edits would not satisfy the requested optimization goal.
